steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 350 °F.
Sift 1 1/2 cups of flour, 2 teaspoons of baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon of salt together.
Cream 1/2 cup of butter in a large bowl.
Add 1 cup of white sugar and 1/2 cup of packed brown sugar and cream well.
Add 2 eggs and 1 teaspoon of vanilla.
Beat until fluffy.
Blend in the dry ingredients.
Stir in 1 cup of chopped almond toffee.
Spread the batter over the bottom of a well-greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake for about 30 minutes.
Cut the cooled blondies into bars 3 inches long and 1 inch wide.
steps.spoken: When the blondies are cool, cut them into bars 3 inches long and 1 inch wide. This makes 3 dozen bars.

source.credit: University of Maryland Cooperative Extension, SNAP-Ed Program

steps.instruction: Cut the 4 squashes into halves.
Remove the seeds from the squash halves.
Place the squash halves in a glass dish.
Cover the dish with plastic wrap.
Microwave on high for 5 minutes.
Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a separate bowl in the microwave.
Mix 2 chopped apples into the melted butter.
Mix in 2 teaspoons of brown sugar and 1/2 teaspoon of cinnamon.
Microwave the apple mixture for 90 seconds.
Spoon the apple filling into each squash half.
Cover the dish.
Microwave on high for 3 minutes, until the squash and apples are tender.
steps.spoken: Microwave on high for 3 to five minutes, until the squash and apples are tender.

source.name: USDA MyPlate Kitchen
source.credit: Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education, ONIE Project

steps.instruction: Rub 1 teaspoon of cumin over the 4 chicken breasts.
Place the chicken in a skillet over medium-high heat.
steps.spoken: Cook the chicken for 6 minutes on this side.

steps.instruction: Flip the chicken and cook the other side for 6 minutes.
steps.spoken: Flip the chicken and cook the other side for 6 minutes, until no pink is left and a thermometer reads 165 °F in the thickest part.

steps.instruction: Remove the chicken from the pan and keep it warm.
Add 5 tablespoons of apricot spread, the lemon juice and 2 tablespoons of water.
Stir over medium heat until smooth.
Spoon the sauce over the chicken.

source.name: NHLBI (NIH)
source.credit: NHLBI, NIH; Stay Young At Heart

steps.instruction: Scrub 4 large potatoes, then cut them into long 1/2-inch strips.
Place the potato strips in 8 cups of ice water.
Cover the bowl and chill for 1 hour.
steps.spoken: Cover the bowl and chill for 1 hour or longer.

steps.instruction: Remove the potato strips and dry them thoroughly.
Preheat the oven to 475 °F.
Put 1 teaspoon each of garlic powder, onion powder and white pepper in a bag.
Add 1 teaspoon of hot pepper flakes and 1/4 teaspoon each of salt and allspice.
Toss the potato strips in the spice mixture.
Put the potato strips in a shallow baking pan.
Brush the potato strips with 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil.
Cover the pan with foil and bake for 15 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake 15 more minutes, turning the fries now and then.
steps.spoken: Remove the foil and keep baking, uncovered, for 15 to twenty more minutes, until golden brown. Turn the fries now and then to brown them on all sides.

source.credit: Delicious Heart-Healthy Latino Recipes/ Platillos Latinos Sabrosos y Saludables, US Department of Health and Human Services, National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

steps.instruction: Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large pot.
Add 2 pounds of cubed lean beef to the pot.
Brown the beef cubes.
Add 1 large onion and 1 finely chopped garlic clove.
Add 1/4 teaspoon of salt, 1/8 teaspoon of black pepper and 1/4 cup of cilantro.
Add enough water to cover the beef.
Cover the pot and cook over low heat until the beef is tender.
steps.spoken: Cover the pot and cook over low heat until the beef is tender when poked with a fork.

steps.instruction: Add 1 can of stewed tomatoes and 2 ounces of tomato paste.
steps.spoken: Add 1 can of stewed tomatoes and 2 ounces of tomato paste. Keep cooking for about 20 minutes.

steps.instruction: Add 2 cans of hominy and cook over low heat, stirring now and then.
steps.spoken: Add 2 cans of hominy and cook over low heat, stirring now and then. Add the hominy and keep cooking over low heat for another 15 minutes, stirring now and then. If the soup is too thick, add water.

source.name: USDA MyPlate Kitchen
source.credit: A Healthier You: Based on the Dietary Guidelines for Americans, US Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion

steps.instruction: Cut 1 pound of lean beef into 1-inch cubes.
Heat 1 teaspoon of oil in a non-stick skillet.
Add 3/4 tablespoon of finely chopped onion.
steps.spoken: Add 3/4 tablespoon of finely chopped onion. Add the onion and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.instruction: Add the cubed beef.
steps.spoken: Add the beef and sauté for 5 more minutes, turning it to brown evenly.

steps.instruction: Remove the beef from the pan and keep it hot.
Add the remaining 1 teaspoon of oil to the pan.
Sauté 1 pound of sliced mushrooms in the pan.
Add the beef and onions back to the pan.
Add 1/4 teaspoon salt, 1 dash black pepper and 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg.
Add 1/2 teaspoon of dried basil.
Gently stir in 1/4 cup beef broth and 1 cup plain yogurt.
Heat gently, but do not boil.
steps.spoken: Heat the pan gently, but do not let it boil.

steps.instruction: Serve with 6 cups of cooked macaroni.

source.name: USDA MyPlate Kitchen
source.credit: California Department of Health Services, California Children’s 5-A-Day Power Play Campaign

steps.instruction: Add 6 small quartered red potatoes to a pot of boiling water over high heat.
steps.spoken: Add 6 small quartered red potatoes to a pot of boiling water over high heat. Cook the potatoes for about 10 minutes, until they are tender.

steps.instruction: Drain the potatoes well and let them cool.
Place the potatoes in a medium bowl.
Mix 1/2 cup of Italian dressing and 1 1/2 teaspoons of mustard in a small bowl.
Mix in 1 tablespoon of parsley, 1/2 teaspoon of garlic salt and 1/4 teaspoon of pepper.
Pour the mixture over the potatoes and toss well.
Carefully stir in 1/2 cup each of chopped green and red bell pepper.
Carefully stir in 1/2 cup of sliced green onion.
Cover the salad and chill until ready to serve.

source.name: USDA MyPlate Kitchen
source.credit: Montana State University Extension Service, Nutrition Education Program

ingredients.name: black beans, 15 ounces, low-sodium, drained and rinsed

steps.instruction: Stir 1/2 cup of onion, 1/2 cup of bell pepper, 1 cup of rice and the beans in a bowl.
Put 1/4 cup of rice vinegar and 1/2 teaspoon of mustard powder in a jar.
Add 1 clove of garlic, 1/2 teaspoon of salt and 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper.
Add 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil to the jar.
Close the lid tightly and shake until the dressing is evenly mixed.
Pour the dressing over the bean mixture and stir to mix evenly.
Chill the salad for 1 hour, then serve it cold.
steps.spoken: Chill the salad for at least one hour, then serve it cold.

steps.instruction: Melt 5 teaspoons of unsalted butter in a pot over medium-low heat.
Once the butter is fully melted, stir in 5 teaspoons of flour.
Keep stirring on medium-low heat until golden and nutty-smelling.
steps.spoken: Keep stirring the flour and butter on medium-low heat until it is lightly golden brown and starts to smell a bit nutty.

steps.instruction: Stir in about 1 cup of the milk until combined.
Repeat with more milk until the sauce is thick.
steps.spoken: Keep adding milk, a cup at a time, until you have a thick sauce and new milk mixes in easily. Never stop stirring.

steps.instruction: Stir in the rest of the milk.
Lower the heat to low and keep stirring.
steps.spoken: Lower the heat to low and keep stirring. Get into the corners of the pot, because the sauce burns easily.

steps.instruction: When the sauce is as thick as you like, add salt and pepper to taste.
Add a pinch of nutmeg, freshly grated if you can.

ingredients.name: tuna steak, cut into 4 portions (3 ounces each)
low-sodium chickpeas, drained and rinsed (or garbanzo beans)
tomato, rinsed and cut into wedges

steps.instruction: Preheat the broiler on high, with the rack 3 inches from the heat.
steps.spoken: Preheat the broiler on high with the rack 3 inches from the heat. You can heat a grill pan on high instead.

steps.instruction: Mix 1 tablespoon each of oil, garlic and oregano with 2 tablespoons of lemon juice.
Brush the mixture over 12 ounces of tuna steak, cut into 4 portions.
Let the tuna marinate for 5 minutes.
steps.spoken: Let the tuna marinate for 5 to ten minutes.

steps.instruction: Mix 1/2 can of chickpeas and 1/2 bag of spinach with 1 tablespoon of lemon juice.
Add 1 tomato cut into wedges, and 1/8 teaspoon each of salt and pepper.
Grill or broil the tuna on high for 3 minutes.
steps.spoken: Grill or broil the tuna on high for 3 to four minutes.

steps.instruction: Flip the tuna and cook the other side for 3 minutes.
steps.spoken: Flip the tuna and cook the other side for 3 to four minutes, until the fish looks opaque and flakes easily with a fork. A thermometer should read 145 °F.

steps.instruction: Serve 1 tuna steak over 1 cup of the salad.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Lower 4 eggs into the boiling water with a spoon.
Fill a bowl with ice and cold water.
Move the eggs into the ice water for 5 minutes.
Peel the eggs and serve.

source.credit: NHLBI, NIH; Heart Healthy Home Cooking African American Style

steps.instruction: Wash 6 medium potatoes and cut them in half.
Put the potatoes in a saucepan of cold water.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 25 minutes, until tender.
steps.spoken: Cover and cook over medium heat for 25 to thirty minutes, until the potatoes are tender.

steps.instruction: Drain the potatoes and let them cool.
Dice the cooled potatoes.
Add 2 chopped celery stalks, 2 chopped scallions and 1 tablespoon of chopped onion.
Add 1/4 cup each of red bell pepper and green bell pepper, coarsely chopped.
Add 1 chopped hard-boiled egg and toss.
In a small bowl, blend 6 tablespoons of mayonnaise and 1 teaspoon of mustard.
Blend in 1/2 teaspoon of salt, 1/4 teaspoon of pepper and 1/4 teaspoon of dill weed.
Pour the dressing over the potato mixture and stir gently to coat.
Chill for at least 1 hour before serving.
